fieldMarks: Legless, with eyelids, external ear openings and lateral grooves; tail usually over twice the snout-vent length; 45-108 cm, the longest lizard in North America.
Adults dark green above with many black lines running from head to tail, yellow below, usually with white marks on the neck and back.
No stripe on the middle of the back and none below the lateral grooves; juveniles tan.
Females greener; males yellowish-green with broader stripes and gold or brown speckles.
behavior: Crepuscular; hunts at dawn, dusk or after rain, mostly burrowing through loose soil; may bask mid-morning or early evening on roads or open ground.
Eats insects (grasshoppers mainly), spiders, worms, slugs and snails, and sometimes bird eggs, snakes and lizards.
Brumates in burrows below the frost line; mostly solitary.
habitat: Moist and dry areas, especially damp grassy areas, pine flatwoods, maritime forest and sandy friable soils near ponds, marshes and estuaries.
range: Atlantic and Gulf Coastal Plains: Florida, most of Georgia and South Carolina, coastal North Carolina and southeastern Virginia, west along the Gulf coast to eastern Louisiana. Not in Canada.

lookalikes.name: Slender glass lizard
lookalikes.howToTell: Slender glass lizard has a dark middorsal stripe or dashes and stripes below the lateral groove; eastern has neither.

lookalikes.name: Snakes (legless look-alikes)
lookalikes.howToTell: Glass lizards have eyelids and ear openings; snakes do not.
